parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for std-only Rust, Cargo plus package-root test15.rs, byte-identical output, C++ argv/stoi behavior, negative count handling, unique-key equal_range semantics, and black-box inference.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned the deliverable and ran implementation locally while a background workflow owned advisory spec, design, and judge phases with multiple subagents.
parallel.implementation: The parent created Cargo.toml, test15.rs, cxx runtime/argv/string shims, and tsl hash/hopscotch modules, then fixed compile-time accessor and warning issues.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: All implementation writes landed in /output under one parent-owned Cargo project; artifact validation found the expected entry, compiled binaries, target output, and module files.
parallel.verification: The parent probed the reference binary, performed differential testing, built via rustc and Cargo, and the official evaluator later passed all 40 testcases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The parent process timed out with an empty final response, and the background workflow was killed with no aggregate judge result, but the produced artifact was complete enough to pass.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, pure-std, Cargo project, package-root entry, CLI/stoi parity, byte-identical output, and black-box reimplementation requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor handled probing, design, implementation, integration, debugging, verification, and final reporting without delegation or subagent handoffs.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote Cargo.toml, test15.rs, cxx_compat.rs, tsl hash/hopscotch/map modules, fixed a Debug derive issue, fixed hop-closer logic, and fixed overflow-triggered rehash behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial project was integrated in /output with the required entry source, executable, Cargo target, and module tree, with no cross-agent workspace ownership.
serial.verification: The serial run performed C++ binary probes, 58 differential cases, Cargo release build, cargo tests, and structural dependency checks before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task-relevant unfinished work remained; the only apparent failed summary was a stale initial evaluator record superseded by the successful retry in status.json.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the core requirements from the prompt and explored exact C++ behavior before and during implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and kept them in one local implementation path.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement coverage difference affected the official outcome; both passed all current tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed advisory work into workflow spec, design, and judge phases while the parent retained direct implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not decompose across agents; the single parent owned every phase end to end.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced an advisory workflow ownership branch that did not exist in serial, but implementation ownership stayed with the parent in both successful artifacts.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs contained the shown C++ program, binary path, black-box rule, and specific output schemas for advisory results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried prompt context directly in the parent trajectory, avoiding child handoff interfaces.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit child brief and structured-output interfaces; serial had no cross-agent interface, but no harmful missing contract affected the final artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent built a multi-module Rust port with cxx shims and tsl hopscotch modules, then adjusted compile issues and semantics.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built a similar multi-module port, fixed compile issues, found an overflow-growth bug through unit tests, and reran checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented a functional port; serial performed an additional local bug-fix cycle before its normal final response, while parallel's artifact still passed official tests despite timeout.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel left the background workflow without a finalized aggregate result after the process timeout killed active judge agents.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve and reached a normal final response after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The material lifecycle difference is the lost workflow result in parallel; it did not change the official pass result because the parent artifact was already sufficient.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote the final /output tree while workflow children mostly read/probed and produced advisory results; no concrete concurrent write collision was proven.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the final /output tree from a single actor and artifact validation found the expected files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had shared read access by advisory children but no observed adverse merge or overwrite; serial had simpler provenance.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed reference probes, differential tests, rustc and Cargo builds, and official evaluation passed 40/40, though a local cargo test command was cut off by the process timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran C++ probes, full differential testing, cargo tests, rebuilds, structural checks, and official evaluation passed 40/40.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial closed the verification loop more cleanly in its own trajectory; parallel still produced a passing artifact but had interrupted local closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a long-running workflow plus parent implementation and hit the global timeout, leaving the workflow killed and final response empty.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in 896.964 agent seconds with returncode 0 and substantial remaining budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's main disadvantage was budget/closure pressure from the background workflow and parent work; serial closed normally.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations passed 40/40. The apparent serial failure in cell/evaluation/summary.json is stale and is superseded by the retry evaluation embedded in serial cell/status.json. The concrete process difference is closure, not correctness: parallel produced a passing artifact while its parent and workflow were terminated before final reporting; serial completed normally.
parallel_contributors: Parent-owned implementation wrote and verified a sufficient artifact before timeout.
Background workflow produced advisory spec/design work but did not return its final judge synthesis.
serial_contributors: Single actor completed probing, implementation, differential testing, unit testing, and final response without delegation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial explicitly found and fixed an overflow-triggered rehash bug during unit testing; parallel's implementation path differed but still passed official tests.
evaluator_effects: Serial cell/evaluation/summary.json is a stale incomplete pre-retry record; current cell/status.json evaluation is the authoritative passing result.

candidates.reason: The parallel parent explicitly owned and executed implementation writes in /output, so implementation was not ownerless.
The parent integrated all final modules into one Cargo project; children were advisory and did not own incompatible component implementations.
The parent assembled the package-root test15.rs, Cargo.toml, modules, and compiled executable; artifact validation found the expected entry.
The parent carried implementation, build, differential testing, and delivery even though the advisory workflow did not finish.
Parent implementation proceeded while the workflow ran; productive work was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight.
Investigation and implementation overlapped after the workflow launch, so implementation was not deferred until all investigation completed.
The indispensable implementation path had the parent actively working on it and produced a passing artifact; no underallocated critical path is shown.
The workflow was broad and long, but the evidence does not isolate excessive fan-out as the direct cause rather than the explicit global timeout killing active judge agents.
No single child was assigned a uniquely overbroad indispensable implementation task; the incomplete work was judge-stage advisory work in a killed workflow.
The child briefs included the shown C++ source, binary path, black-box constraint, and explicit task obligations; no known requirement omission caused unusable work.
Children produced advisory specs and designs rather than separately owned code components requiring a missing interoperability contract.
No known finding is shown disappearing through summary or transfer and causing repeated or wrong downstream work.
Large structured child outputs existed, but the parent did not receive a bulky completed aggregate that it failed to reduce at a decision point.
No receiver is shown consuming superseded workspace or requirement information and acting inconsistently because of it.
Although design agents explored different approaches, no incompatible returned contracts remained unadjudicated in the final artifact.
Parallel made no normal whole-task completion decision; final response was empty, and official evaluation passed the artifact.
One judge retry started after a stall, but the retry did not proceed far enough to show repeated prior work without inherited state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The executed background workflow was explicitly killed with result null while judge agents were still active, losing the planned aggregate judge result.
candidates.realized_consequence: The workflow's judge-stage aggregate result was never finalized or returned to the parent; the parallel final response was empty although the artifact passed.
candidates.near_match_reason: No completed verifier finding was trapped below the parent; the judge agents were interrupted before finalizing, making cancellation the direct boundary.

candidates.reason: A complete deliverable artifact was already produced and passed; the unfinished item was advisory workflow synthesis, not a promotable candidate left unplaced.
No child implementation change was merged after integrated verification without a later verification step.
No delegated implementation was completed and then left unjoined; implementation was parent-owned and child outputs were advisory.
Judge/verifier agents had not completed a concrete finding before the workflow was killed, so the missing aggregate return is downstream of early termination.
The parent had already taken over the required implementation and produced a passing artifact; the cancelled workflow was advisory, not a required child failure left unhandled.
No completed workflow aggregate result was available to the parent and ignored; the workflow result field was null.
The parent did not simply wait blindly; it actively implemented, built, probed, and tested while the workflow ran in the background.
No concurrent agents wrote competing implementation files or overlapping behavior designs into the final tree.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source file with a required reconciliation.
No child-owned non-entry source was replaced or wholesale rewritten by another actor.
The parent wrote the entry source and executable; no other live actor owned or replaced that deliverable.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced another actor's final-tree work or invalidated provenance.
Although advisory children could inspect /output, multiple live agents are not shown writing the shared implementation workspace and causing unstable provenance.
Children reading parent-created /output files did not contaminate final execution or verification; no generated artifact was consumed as a false reference environment.

retained_patterns.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing
retained_patterns.reason: The parent launched a background workflow; the global timeout returned 143 and the workflow state ended killed with result null while judge agents were still active. This lost the planned aggregate judge result even though the parent artifact passed.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The workflow's judge-stage aggregate result was never finalized or returned to the parent; the parallel final response was empty although the artifact passed.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: No completed verifier finding was trapped below the parent; the judge agents were interrupted before finalizing, making cancellation the direct boundary.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Fan-out Budget Exhaustion, Missing Verifier Return, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered for the same killed-workflow chain and rejected because Early Child Termination is the direct observed boundary.
Late Finalization was rejected because the task artifact was already assembled and passing, while the unfinished workflow output was advisory.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; the only realized parallel coordination harm was the killed active workflow.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The timeout/cancellation chain was retained once and was not split into budget, missing-return, takeover, or monitoring labels.
